industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the case for Overweight stronger than at any time since the row was set and still not taken. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-11-06 against 2026-09-04, not week on week: A now, C prior: healthcare is the defensive the market is paying for, with Medtech capital goods A, Pharma/biotech B, Medtech consumables B and Pharma manufacturing services B. Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only) pays large, proven, cash-yielding cases, which is the Pharma/biotech row (B) and Hospitals (B). Held at C because the industry letter adds the same 30% weight to clinical-stage biotech (D, relative strength F) and capex-cyclical medical equipment as to large pharma, no source spoke to pharmaceuticals against medical technology this week, and eleven of the top 40 on the starting score are already healthcare names. Counter-case for B: two readings two months apart at A with the regime's rotation confirmed on every window; for D: a crowded destination. To B if a source carries a healthcare read with the industry's relative strength holding A or B.

sector.why: Underweight, set deliberately this week (the carried B was inherited from the old Pharma/biotech row, whose reason was large, proven, cash-yielding pharma; clinical-stage biotech is the opposite case). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): unproven, cash-burning, long-duration, financed at the margin, the profile the Fragility axis and the discount-rate read say the market is refusing this week, and no source spoke to biotech. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: F now, C prior, agrees. Counter-case: seven stocks, binary outcomes that do not follow the discount rate, and the sector is small enough that one trial result reorders it; the Fragility axis already scores their size, so this row carries one notch, not two.

memo.verdict: PARK, with high conviction. Do not progress Idorsia Ltd (IDIA-CH) to Early-Stage Assessment on the current evidence. The memo adopts, rather than argues against, the recommendation carried in the on-disk risks report, whose section 14 "Stage Progression" states: "Hold recommendation: neutral rating stances are maintained pending concrete commercial inflection or clinical study readouts." Hold-and-watch translated into Viewforth's five-stage funnel is park, because Viewforth does not hold a stock it has not progressed, and the report's stated precondition, concrete commercial inflection, has not occurred. The park rests on three tests that fail independently: case simplicity at F, both Element E8 negative guardrails at F, and case riskiness at F. A single failing test would be arguable; three unrelated failures are not. Named conditions for progression, all five currently unmet: (1) Q3 2026 QUVIVIQ net sales above CHF 55m and Q4 2026 above CHF 60m, the thresholds named in the earnings review's own change-my-mind test; (2) a binding TRYVIO co-promotion agreement with upfront payments above CHF 50m and at least mid-teens royalty rates, announced by 31 March 2027; (3) resolution of the CHF 250m Cilag convertible maturing June 2027 with realised dilution below 10%; (4) United States quarterly net sales breaking above CHF 12m, ending the CHF 9m plateau; (5) positive Phase 2 CCR6 antagonist psoriasis data in Q4 2026 showing PASI-75 response above 40%. Named bear-case confirmation triggers, which would move the verdict from park to kill rather than back toward progression: Q3 2026 QUVIVIQ sales below CHF 50m, no TRYVIO partnering announcement by March 2027, or a CCR6 Phase 2 readout missing its primary endpoint.
case: The case for parking runs in four steps.

Step one: the change forces are real, and the memo says so before it says anything negative. External change is dated and commercially transmissible. QUVIVIQ secured a NICE recommendation as first-line pharmacological treatment for chronic insomnia with access extending to over 85% of Integrated Care Boards. Following French Official Gazette inclusion for retail and hospital reimbursement, it reached 14.4% new-to-brand share within ten months among specialists. German authorities removed the legacy four-week prescription limit, recognising QUVIVIQ as the sole approved long-term chronic insomnia treatment, with quarterly unit volumes growing over 20% sequentially and 34m tablets sold in Q2 2026. On 11 August 2026 the DEA proposed reclassifying the dual orexin antagonist class from Schedule IV to Schedule V. Internal change is equally real: a permanent commercial chief executive from 1 October 2026, an operating cost base cut from CHF 654m in 2023 to a guided CHF 330m for FY26, and the completed Pharmakon refinancing. Neither peer with a master digest shows comparable positive external change; Hikma is absorbing three consecutive profit warnings and Merck KGaA faces a Mavenclad patent cliff guided at minus 3% to minus 6% organic.

Step two: the base those forces act on fails on all five Core Questions. Headwinds are present on every value-chain axis, not absent: generic zolpidem at nearly 99% of prescription volume against a total dual orexin class of roughly 0.9m United States prescriptions; payer rebate pressure that cut gross margin 930 basis points; roughly 65% of operating costs in Swiss francs with no formal accounting hedges; Eisai's Dayvigo at JPY 44.5bn FY25 sales growing 20% and relaunching in the United States by telehealth across over 30 states; and AstraZeneca's baxdrostat, acquired for up to USD 2.5bn with a USD 6.5bn peak sales target. The base is under-invested rather than well-invested: 20 virtual representatives against an expert-stated threshold of 250 for an independent United States sales force, zero owned chemical manufacturing, and capital expenditure of CHF 9m in each of 2023 and 2024. Delivery is congruent on the top line and incongruent below it: product sales up 62%, but non-GAAP operating loss widened from CHF 15m to CHF 54m and US-GAAP net loss expanded to CHF 153m. The mispricing is gone: at CHF 5.915 the shares sit 33.5% above the CHF 4.43 dashboard consensus target, above HC Wainwright's CHF 5.00 and above Deutsche Bank's CHF 5.50, having risen 145% from the CHF 2.415 low. And no usable multiple exists, because forward earnings per share are negative CHF 0.2445 and the reported ratio of (16.9)x at percentile 0 reflects losses rather than cheapness.
counter_case: The counter-case is strong on three fronts and the memo carries all three at full force.

First, the technical dissent. Master Rating MR1 grades technical momentum at B. The relative-strength percentile is 98, the 200-day average has risen for twelve consecutive months, the price sits 39.0% above it, and the twelve-month relative return is 122%. In a change-driven, momentum-supported process, that is a real signal, and the memo records it as the single strongest argument against parking rather than burying it. Short interest has fallen out of the Swiss top-ten shorted list and OTC short interest fell 12.6% to 6.31m shares, so positioning has moved with the price. The memo rejects the argument only on the ground that the price now exceeds every published target, so the technical strength has consumed the valuation headroom rather than created it.
triggers: Progression triggers, five, all currently unmet: Q3 2026 QUVIVIQ net sales above CHF 55m and Q4 2026 above CHF 60m; a binding TRYVIO co-promotion agreement with upfront payments above CHF 50m and at least mid-teens royalty rates by 31 March 2027; resolution of the CHF 250m Cilag convertible maturing June 2027 with realised dilution below 10%; United States quarterly net sales breaking above CHF 12m; positive Phase 2 CCR6 antagonist psoriasis data in Q4 2026 showing PASI-75 response above 40%.
Kill triggers, three: Q3 2026 QUVIVIQ sales below CHF 50m; no TRYVIO partnering announcement by March 2027; a CCR6 Phase 2 readout missing its primary endpoint.

Monitoring instruments, two, both drawn from the earnings review's own set: weekly IQVIA United States prescription tracking for QUVIVIQ, with 4,500 weekly total prescriptions as the traction threshold; and monthly IQVIA panel data across France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom, with 15% sequential monthly volume growth as the primary-care penetration threshold. The named false-friend diagnostic is a gap between reported sales and IQVIA prescription data, which reveals inventory channel stuffing.

Regulatory calendar: DEA comments due September 2026, a final rule realistically delayed to H1 2027, state implementation stretching into 2028. Clinical calendar: lucerastat pivotal Fabry kidney biopsy study begins Q3 2026 with filing not before 2029 and a 20% probability of success assigned by HC Wainwright; CCR6 antagonist Phase 2 psoriasis readout Q4 2026; cenerimod Phase 3 OPUS readout in systemic lupus erythematosus expected H1 2027; selatogrel Phase 3 enrolment completion slated end-2026.

What would make this a progress call is not a higher price but evidence that the driver count has collapsed and that equity holders can capture the value. The simplest version: a signed TRYVIO partnership plus a resolved June 2027 convertible would remove two of the six drivers and the solvency-shaped constraint at once.

If progressing, the Early-Stage Assessment must open with two builds the memo names: a full Element E3 valuation on a sum-of-the-parts basis, because no earnings multiple exists; and an Element E17 capital-constraining test on the waterfall note structure.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
